newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Oct-Dec domestic PC shipments up 10% yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan Oct-Dec domestic PC shipments up 10% yr/yr.

text.p: Japan's domestic personal computer shipments rose 10 percent to 1.72 million units during the October-December period of 1996 over the same period a year earlier, a trade association announced on Tuesday.
It said the value of shipments rose 13 percent in the same period from a year earlier to 429.4 billion yen.
Shipments for the current fiscal year, ending on March 31, may fall short of the target of 7.5 million units, the Japan Electronic Industry Development Association said.

On reasons for the possible failure to reach its target, the trade body said a delay in the launch of PCs fitted with the new MMX chip made by Intel Corp and with DVD-ROMs meant demand did not rise as quickly as expected, it said.
Such PCs had been expected to appear on the market in the third quarter, but they did not do so until January.
The year-earlier figure was also boosted by the introduction of Windows 95, an association official said.

In the October-December quarter of fiscal 1995, shipments of all-in-one type desktop PCs for home use grew 200 percent, helped in part by the introduction of Windows 95. Growth in the same quarter of 1996 was only one percent, partly because consumers held back on purchases of such PCs in anticipation of the launch of MMX, he said.

"Japan will easily clear the 1996/97 shipment target in terms of value of 1.6 trillion yen because the unit price of PCs is higher. If you use your common sense, attaining the 1996/97 volume target of 7.5 million units would be difficult," the official, a spokesman for the body, told a news conference.
The association said domestic shipments from January to December 1996 totalled 6.8 million units, up 33 percent from the previous year.
For the next fiscal year, starting on April, it said it was keeping its target for the volume of shipments unchanged for the time being at 9.3 million units.
"We expect some favourable factors to support sales next year, such as the introduction of Windows NT 4.0 software," the spokesman said.
